examples.text: an act of goodwill
That best portion of a good man's life, / His little, nameless, unremembered acts / Of kindness and of love.
The seeds of plants are not at first in act, but in possibility, what they afterward grow to be.

glosses: Something done once and for all, as distinguished from a work.
A product of a legislative body, a statute.

examples.text: But was it responsible governance to pass the Longitude Act without other efforts to protect British seamen? Or might it have been subterfuge—a disingenuous attempt to shift attention away from the realities of their life at sea.

glosses: (In the United States) A legislative proposal, a bill that has not yet become law.

examples.text: Under current law, employers can drag out the union election process... Under the PRO Act, workers and the NLRB set union election procedures. The employer is not involved.
He was caught in the act of stealing.

glosses: A formal or official record of something done.
A division of a theatrical performance.

examples.text: “H'm !” he said, “so, so—it is a tragedy in a prologue and three acts. I am going down this afternoon to see the curtain fall for the third time on what […] will prove a good burlesque ; but it all began dramatically enough. It was last Saturday […] that two boys, playing in the little spinney just outside Wembley Park Station, came across three large parcels done up in American cloth. […]”
The pivotal moment in the play was in the first scene of the second act.

glosses: A performer or performers in a show.

examples.text: Which act did you prefer? The soloist or the band?
The minute you let it be known you're planning a sales campaign everybody wants to get into the act.

glosses: A display of behaviour meant to deceive.

examples.text: to put on an act
He said, "I'm just curious, is this for real or just an act? / Can't tell if you love or hate me, never met someone like that"

glosses: A thesis maintained in public, in some English universities, by a candidate for a degree, or to show the proficiency of a student.

examples.text: If you don’t act soon, you will be in trouble.
that we act our temporal affairs with a deſire no greater than our neceſſity
Industry doth beget by producing good habits, and facility of acting things expedient for us to do.
Uplifted hands that at convenient times / Could act extortion and the worst of crimes.
I started acting at the age of eleven in my local theatre.

glosses: Of a play: to be acted out (well or badly).

examples.text: But whatever types he assumes, the need to have a good play which acts delightfully well before the audience, and to their delectation, is the dominant thrust. If the play acts well, the director gets the credits.

glosses: To behave in a certain manner for an indefinite length of time.

examples.text: A dog which acts aggressively is likely to bite.
I believe that Bill’s stuck-up because of the way that he acts.
He’s acting strangely—I think there’s something wrong with him.

glosses: To convey an appearance of being.

examples.text: He acted unconcerned so the others wouldn’t worry.

glosses: To do something that causes a change binding on the doer.

examples.text: act on behalf of John
High-pressure oxygen acts on the central nervous system and may cause convulsions or death.
Gravitational force acts on heavy bodies.
He’s been acting Shakespearean leads since he was twelve.
He acted the angry parent, but was secretly amused.
With acted fear the villain thus pursued.

glosses: To carry out work as a legal representative in relation to a particular legal matter.

examples.text: A lawyer cannot act until they have been formally instructed by their client.

glosses: To possess an action onto (some other structure). Examples include the group action of a group on a set, the action of a ring on a module by scalar multiplication, and the action of a group or algebra on a vector space via a representation.

examples.text: This group acts on the circle, so it can't be left-orderable!

glosses: To move to action; to actuate; to animate.

examples.text: Self-love, the spring of motion, acts the soul.

examples.text: Épater un chien.
— Vase à pied épaté.

Elle se servait pour étaler la pâte d’une petite spatule de plastique qui ne manquait jamais de se briser sous la pression et qu’elle remplaçait alors par des allumettes dont elle épatait l’extrémité non soufrée.

glosses: Faire tomber les quatre fers en l’air.

examples.text: Je me suis épaté lourdement.

En six coups de pied il fit rouler au milieu de la route les six grotesques fantoches, qui s’épatèrent sur la poudre avec ces gestes irrésistiblement comiques de marionnettes dont on a abandonné les fils.
Je me revois tout chétif, tout mièvre, suivant les cours du catéchisme, où j’arrivais bon premier. Ma piété, mon application épataient le bon curé.
Déjà quand j’étais petit garçon, répond Siméon, j’épatais mes parents en composant des itinéraires dans le jardin pour mes modèles réduits de voitures.
